finish.summary: I built a small sewing caddy from three hex cells set in a triangle, each with a full-depth bin. The build check passes with no rule issues and no parts colliding, and it has 18 parts in total. One cell has 3 compartments for small items like pins, needles and buttons. Another has 2 compartments for spools of thread. The third is one open bin for scissors, a tape measure or fabric scraps. Open faces have end caps and the joints are bolted so the cells stay together. There are no sewing props to show it in use, so I staged it with a pen, tweezers, a tape measure and a marker. A pencil standing upright wouldn't stay put in the compartments, so I left it out. The tweezers are barely visible from above.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
